sections.content: How many people are "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers"?

8,850 people

were counted on the census as "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Glass and ceramics workers, form, shape, decorate, smooth and polish glassware, earthenware, refractory goods, clay bricks and other ceramic goods.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" included:

  • construction operatives (other)
  • gardeners and landscape gardeners
  • parking and civil enforcement occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" there were more men than women (61.9% compared with 38.1%).

This means "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 61.9% and women made up 38.1% of "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" included:

  • protective service associate professionals (other)
  • inspectors of standards and regulations
  • food, drink and tobacco process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers", 11.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (72.7% compared with 27.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (64.8%) than self-employed (35.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Stoke-on-Trent, this is in the same region of the West Midlands.
